coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 31 days out and sitting at 55/100 recovery—moderate, not ideal. Your resting HR is 11 bpm above your 30-day average (76 vs 65.3), which signals incomplete recovery from last week's 31.1 miles. Today is a Tuesday quality slot, but the data doesn't support a hard interval session. Run 45–50 min easy in Z2 (roughly 140–150 bpm based on your recent efforts), focusing on smooth movement and terrain familiarity—think rolling alpine-grade gravel or trail. This keeps the taper momentum without digging deeper into your deficit.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Last night you slept 10.4 hours at 90.8% efficiency—excellent—but that sleep depth suggests your body was playing catch-up. Prioritize carbs heavily today: aim for 6–8g per kg bodyweight, distributed across 4–5 meals. With elevated resting HR and moderate recovery, glycogen replenishment is your front-line recovery tool. Breakfast should include oats, toast, or rice; post-run, hit 40–60g fast carbs + 15–20g protein within 30 minutes. Skip fasted running in taper; you need calories to stabilize HR and adaptation.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your 10.4-hour sleep night was a response to accumulated fatigue—trust it, but don't expect it every night. Tonight, aim for 8.5–9 hours with consistency. Your 30-day sleep average of 8.11 hours is solid for an ultra runner, but the spike tells me you've been underdoing recovery sleep during build. No HRV data available, so use resting HR as your check: if it stays above 72 bpm tomorrow morning, extend the easy day further. Add 10 min of mobility (hip flexors, calves, TFL) before bed—alpine 50K terrain demands ankle stability under fatigue.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the taper sweet spot: enough time to sharpen, not enough to spiral into doubt. Your last hard effort (12.04 mi / 1457 ft vert at 132 bpm) was solid, and it proves you're fit. The next 31 days are about protecting that fitness and arriving at Kranjska Gora eager, not exhausted. Today's easy run is non-negotiable—the race will demand every ounce of specificity and durability you've built. Lean into the taper's quiet rhythm. Your day job travels will disrupt sleep and stress; use that as fuel for discipline, not an excuse to overtrain.
